Correlated errors between the arms of a benchmark

Source: R/core-bench-errcorr.R
hr_error_correlation.Rd

Says how far the arms of an hr_benchmark() fail on the same items, and with the same wrong answer, and draws a sample of the items every arm got wrong for a person to check by hand. It reads only the benchmark's rows and sends nothing.

Usage

hr_error_correlation(
  bench,
  strata = NULL,
  n_strata = 3L,
  n_check = 10L,
  held_out = TRUE,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

bench

An hr_bench from hr_benchmark() with at least two arms.

strata

NULL to stratify by difficulty, or each item's stratum: a vector named by item, or one value per item in the order of unique(bench$item).

n_strata

How many difficulty strata, when strata is NULL: a whole number from 1 to 10, default 3. Fewer are made when the items take fewer distinct difficulties.

n_check

How many items every arm got wrong to sample for a hand check: a whole number, 0 or more, default 10.

held_out

TRUE (the default) reads only the rows that count as evidence (reportable, so not the dev split); FALSE reads every row.

seed

The seed of the private random stream the sample is drawn with; the caller's random state is left as it was.

Value

A list of class hr_error_correlation:

phi

One row per pair of arms and stratum: arm_a, arm_b, stratum, items, both_wrong, phi (NA where undefined).

pairs

One row per pair of arms: arm_a, arm_b, items, phi_pooled, both_wrong, both_answered (of those, the items where both gave an outcome), same_wrong and same_wrong_rate.

check

The hand-check sample: item and one column per arm holding its wrong outcome.

all_wrong

How many items every arm got wrong.

strata

Each item's stratum, named by item.

q3

Why Yen's Q3 is not given.

Details

Each arm is reduced to one result per item: an error when it was wrong on more than half of its scored runs of the item. Items with no label (every correct NA) are left out.

Phi within difficulty strata

For each pair of arms, the phi coefficient (the correlation of two 0/1 error indicators over the items) within each stratum of item difficulty. Two arms both wrong on the hard items are correlated for that reason alone; within a stratum of items of like difficulty, what is left is the shared blind spot. Difficulty is the share of all the arms' scored runs on an item that were wrong, cut into n_strata groups at its quantiles, unless strata gives each item's stratum (as hr_reference()'s strata do). phi_pooled is the mean of the strata's phi weighted by their items, over strata where phi is defined (both arms right on some items and wrong on others). Because difficulty is read from the same runs, the strata are a coarse adjustment, not an independent one.

Same wrong answer

For each pair, of the items both got wrong where both gave an answer (outcome not NA), the share where they gave the same wrong answer (each arm's most frequent wrong outcome on the item, compared after case and surrounding space are set aside). Kim et al. (2025, "Correlated errors in large language models") report this rate for models that share a provider or architecture.

Hand-check sample

Up to n_check items every arm got wrong, drawn at random with seed, with each arm's wrong outcome, for a person to read. Unanimous errors are where a label can be the thing that is wrong.

Yen's Q3, the residual correlation of a one-parameter item response model fitted as a mixed model, is not computed: it would need a mixed-model package (lme4) that harnessr does not depend on. $q3 says so.

See also

hr_benchmark(), hr_report(), vignette("evaluate")

Examples

ref <- hr_reference(sprintf("q%02d", 1:12), labels = rep("yes", 12),
                    cluster = sprintf("c%02d", 1:12), split = "test")
says <- function(name, wrong_on) hr_arm(name, function(item, ctx) {
  if (item %in% wrong_on) "no" else "yes"
})
arms <- list(says("arm_a", c("q01", "q02", "q03")),
             says("arm_b", c("q01", "q02", "q04")))
bench <- suppressWarnings(hr_benchmark(arms, ref, runs = 1, client = NULL))
ec <- hr_error_correlation(bench, n_strata = 1)
ec$pairs
#>   arm_a arm_b items phi_pooled both_wrong both_answered same_wrong
#> 1 arm_a arm_b    12  0.5555556          2             2          2
#>   same_wrong_rate
#> 1               1
ec$check
#>   item arm_a arm_b
#> 1  q01    no    no
#> 2  q02    no    no
